missions.title: Outbound
missions.briefing: Reyes here, Tereshkova science. Nobody has ever looked at this system from closer than a telescope on Earth. Start with a long-range scan from where we are, then take us out and chart two more bodies: every orbit we enter gets a full sensor sweep.

objectives.text: Run a long-range scan from the start orbit
objectives.hint: Select the ship on the SYSTEM display and press SCAN: it identifies every body in range.
Set a course for a body: once in orbit, the sensor sweep charts it in a few seconds.

missions.debrief: Three bodies charted, and the first long-range picture of the whole system. Earth has it already: they are asking for more.

missions.title: Eyes Everywhere
missions.briefing: We can't be everywhere at once, but our survey satellites can. Leave one at two different bodies: they keep reading them for good after we have gone.

objectives.text: Place survey satellites at 2 different bodies
objectives.hint: In orbit of a body: SATELLITE on the ship's card. One per body.

missions.debrief: Both satellites are reporting. That's live data from two worlds at once, without us sitting in orbit.

missions.title: Close Look
missions.briefing: The big ones are the strangest, and {target} is the one I want: the nearest gas giant or ice world we haven't swept, or the biggest body out here if there is none. Take us into orbit and give it a full sensor sweep for live data.

objectives.hint: Set a course for {target} ({target.distance} s) and stay in orbit until the sweep is done.

missions.debrief: Beautiful data. Storm bands, rings of ice, magnetic fields like nothing on the charts at home.

missions.title: Wreck at the Edge
missions.briefing: Reyes. The long-range picture has a smear past the last orbit, where nothing should be. It reads like a ship that came apart. Fly out, sweep the debris and bring back her black box: whoever she was, she came a long way to end up there.

objectives.text: Fly out to the contact past the last orbit and identify it
objectives.hint: Set course for the contact past the last orbit ({field.distance} s), then SCAN it from within range.
SWEEP THE FIELD: the box turns up first. The hull wears inside the field, the tractor must work and the hold needs a free container (jettison a used probe or satellite if it is full).

missions.debrief: The recorder plays. She was the Sable Crane, a prospector out of Luna, and her last entries are about a rock in the belt that rang hollow under the drills. Reyes wants that rock.

missions.title: Hollow Rock
missions.briefing: The Sable Crane's log names three rocks in the belt, and one of them rang hollow. Survey them until one reads hollow, then send a team into the cavity: if her crew found something in there, it is still there.

objectives.text: Survey the belt contacts until one reads hollow
objectives.hint: Fly to each marked contact and SCAN it: the card says what it is. One of the three is hollow.
Hold position at the hollow rock and COME ALONGSIDE.

objectives.text: Send an away team into the cavity and bring them back
objectives.hint: AWAY TEAM: Defense lowers the loss chance, a Science medic turns losses into injuries. Leaving the rock calls them back.

missions.debrief: Inside the rock: the Sable Crane's forward camp, and under it something older that nobody from Earth built. Reyes has a lot of questions and, for once, some answers.

missions.title: A Faint Signal
missions.briefing: Something just came through the static: a faint, regular signal from {signal}, the farthest body out. It isn't natural. Take us there and sweep the area.

objectives.hint: It's {signal.distance} s out. The beacon on the system plot marks it.

message.text: Reyes: In orbit of {signal}. Hold here while the sweep runs: the signal is getting stronger.

objectives.hint: Stay in orbit until the sensor sweep is done.

missions.debrief: It's an old beacon, a probe's distress transponder, still ticking after decades. Earth is very interested in who left it here.

missions.title: The Whole Map
missions.briefing: Moreau, Earth Mission Control. You have done more in a few hours than our telescopes did in a century. Finish the job: chart every body in the system, moons and belts included.

objectives.text: Chart every body in the system
objectives.hint: Every body you haven't swept yet is grey on the system plot: visit each one.

missions.debrief: The whole map. Every planet, every moon, every rock, charted by the Tereshkova. This chapter of the survey is closed, and the charts go out to every ship that comes after you.
